$$\begin{aligned}
T_U={}&
\bigl(\{0,1\}\times\{1,\ldots,b\}\bigr)\\

Thus its endpoint degrees are exactly one and three.Both descriptions are preserved by all eight permitted lattice symmetries. They therefore supply the necessary role classification without a dimension cutoff.The completeness adapter is also sound. Suppose an original support  $s$ , absent from the currently retained endpoint union, already has at least two retained endpoint neighbours. Those neighbours remain occupied in every extension. Hence  $s$  cannot remain outside the complete endpoint union, where its support condition would require exactly one occupied neighbour. It must belong to a unique original, by endpoint disjointness.Moreover, a neighbour already occupied by a retained original cannot be an internal endpoint neighbour of that new owner. This is the justification for the “only north” and “only east” arguments. $$a+8(n-2)+7=a+8(n-1)-1,$$

Hence the owner must be a full U.Normalization of every possible U orientationLet  $k\ge4$  be its even near depth. Its near stem occupies
$$\{(2,c):2\le c\le k+2\}.$$
If  $k\ge W$ , it reaches the opposite wall. If  $k=W-2$ , it reaches  $B_i$ ’s opposite stem at column  $W$ . Parity therefore gives

This normalization covers both original terminal choices. The normalization therefore does not silently choose a different matching or support set.At  $k=W-4$ , the outer bar contains  $(4,W-2)$ , an endpoint of the right upper rotor. Consequently,
$$k\le W-6.$$

This support has occupied west, east and south neighbours on  $A$ , this U, and  $B_{i+1}$ . It therefore forces a north-terminal owner. The same all-U and two-rotor exclusions used for the lower mode apply: a U hits  $(4,1)$ , and both rotor records hit  $(5,0)$ .Thus  $f=k$  is impossible. Since the depths are even,
$$\boxed{4\le f\le k-2,\qquad k\ge6.}$$
This step legitimately applies the support rule to the newly identified original. It uses that original’s immutable canonical support, not an inferred or reassigned support.Distinct owners and the width frontierWithin one gap, the two forced points
$$x_L=(2,2),\qquad x_R=(2,W-1)$$
must both be terminals of any hypothetical common owner. But a breadth-six U in the forced orientation has its terminals in rows  $2$  and  $7$ . It cannot own both forced points in row  $2$ .Owners from different gaps are also distinct: each classified endpoint set is contained in rows  $a_i+2,\ldots,a_i+7$ , while the forced rows in different gaps differ by at least eight.The two near stems are
$$[2,k_L+2],\qquad [W-1-k_R,W-1]$$
in row  $2$ . Their endpoint disjointness is equivalent to

and hence to
$$\boxed{k_L+k_R\le W-4.}$$
Because  $f\le k-2$ , the entire left endpoint set lies in columns  $[2,k_L+2]$ , and the right endpoint set lies in the reflected interval. Thus this same inequality separates their whole endpoint sets.It follows that
$$W-4\ge k_L+k_R\ge12,$$
so  $W\ge16$ . It also gives the stronger individual bound
$$\boxed{k_L,k_R\le W-10.}$$
That stronger bound is precisely what removes the single-owner exception from actual pairs.5. The canonical escape-U charge is exactly  $-5$ Put
$$C=k+2,\qquad \ell=C-f,\qquad h=\frac{k+f}{2}.$$
Applying the stated chart to the canonical original gives the complete endpoint description:
$$\begin{array}{ll}
\text{row }2:& 2,\ldots,C,\\
\text{rows }3,4,5,6:& C-1,C,\\
\text{row }7:& \ell,\ldots,C.
\end{array}$$
Its immutable supports are exactly
$$\begin{aligned}
&\{(1,c):c=2,4,\ldots,C\},\\
&\{(8,c):c=\ell,\ell+2,\ldots,C\},\\
&\{(2,1),(7,\ell-1)\},\\
&\{(3,c):c=3,5,\ldots,C-3\},\\
&\{(6,c):c=\ell+1,\ell+3,\ldots,C-3\}.
\end{aligned}$$
This agrees with the supplied support list.The canonical matching has three top-bar edges, two inner-bar edges, and  $k/2+f/2$  stem edges:
$$|M|=5+h.$$
The endpoint tiles are exhaustively:Tile top rowTile left columns $2$  $2,4,\ldots,C$  $4$  $C-2,C$  $6$  $\ell,\ell+2,\ldots,C$ Their number is
$$\left(\frac{k}{2}+1\right)+2+
\left(\frac{f}{2}+1\right)=4+h.$$
Only the row- $3$  and row- $6$  supports lie inside these endpoint tiles. Their respective counts are
$$\frac{k}{2}-1,\qquad \frac{f}{2}-1.$$
The two axial supports lie immediately outside the relevant tile-column ranges; the row- $1$  and row- $8$  supports lie in different tile rows. Therefore the support count is  $h-2$ , and
$$\operatorname{charge}
=(5+h)+(h-2)-2(4+h)
=\boxed{-5}.$$
Each escape U contributes exactly  $5$  to  $N+S$ .6. The single-owner boundary exception is genuine and exhaustiveConsider one left escape U against the common retained-plus-upper-rotor baseline, with
$$6\le k\le W-6,\qquad 4\le f\le k-2.$$
Its endpoint tiles have top rows  $2,4,6$ . In these tile rows, the retained U endpoints occupy tile columns  $0$  and  $W$ . The escape U does not meet those tile columns. The retained horizontal bars lie in tile rows  $0$  and  $8$ .Thus there is no intratile contact with a retained full U.Contact with the left upper rotorThe only common physical tile is  $(2,2)$ . Its occupied cells are
$$U:(2,2),(2,3),\qquad R_L:(3,2).$$
The fourth cell  $(3,3)$  is absent, so this is not a new full tile.There is exactly one cross adjacency. Its U-originating direction is an event:
$$U:(2,2)\longrightarrow R_L:(3,2).$$
The reverse direction targets the rotor’s immutable support  $x=(2,2)$  and is excluded.Contact with the right upper rotorThe right rotor’s endpoint tiles in tile rows  $2$  and  $6$  lie beyond the escape U’s footprint. In tile row  $4$ , the only possible common tile is
$$(4,W-4).$$
The escape U meets it exactly when  $C=W-4$ , equivalently  $k=W-6$ .That tile then contains
$$U:(4,W-4),(5,W-4),\qquad
R_R:(4,W-3).$$
Again, only three cells are occupied. Its unique cross adjacency contributes
$$U:(4,W-4)\longrightarrow R_R:(4,W-3).$$
The reverse direction targets the right rotor’s immutable support  $(4,W-4)$ .These are all common tiles, so the enumeration exhausts both new mixed full tiles and cross events. Hence
$$\Delta|\mathcal F|=0,\qquad
\Delta|E|=1+[k=W-6],$$
and
$$\boxed{\Delta\Phi_{\rm single}=4-[k=W-6].}$$
In particular,  $W=16,k=10,f=4$  has gain  $3$ . Its exceptional event is
$$U:(4,12)\longrightarrow R_R:(4,13).$$
This is a valid counterexample to an unrestricted single-owner gain- $4$  assertion. The supplied note correctly includes it.For actual opposite owners, however,  $k_L,k_R\le W-10$ . Neither member can reach  $k=W-6$ , so each actual owner individually gains  $4$  against the common baseline.7. Tight-band correction and simultaneous nonreuseLet the left outer bar be at
$$C=k_L+2$$
and the right outer bar at
$$D=W-1-k_R.$$
Here  $C$  is even and  $D$  is odd, and
$$D-C=W-3-(k_L+k_R).$$
Slack pairsIf  $k_L+k_R<W-4$ , even parity gives
$$D-C\ge3.$$
The left U’s rightmost tile column is  $C$ , while the right U’s leftmost tile column is  $D-1\ge C+2$ . Their physical tile footprints are disjoint.There are no cooperative full tiles or cross events, and the pair gain is  $8$ .Tight pairsIf  $k_L+k_R=W-4$ , then  $D=C+1$ . The two outer bars occupy adjacent columns  $C,C+1$  in every row  $2,\ldots,7$ .They create exactly three mixed full tiles:
$$(2,C),\qquad(4,C),\qquad(6,C).$$
The band is away from the retained walls and gate rotors:  $k_L,k_R\ge6$  places it strictly in the central region. In either single-U inventory, each of these tiles has only one occupied column. Thus all three full tiles are genuinely cooperative additions.There are six horizontal cross edges, one in each row  $2,\ldots,7$ . Both source-labelled directions count for every edge:All left-U supports have column at most  $C$ , so none excludes a target at  $C+1$ .All right-U supports have column at least  $C+1$ , so none excludes a target at  $C$ .Therefore there are exactly twelve cross events.No other tile column is shared. Vertical cross adjacencies are impossible because the two endpoint sets lie in disjoint column half-planes. The correction is exactly
$$2\cdot3-12=\boxed{-6}.$$
A tight pair consequently gains
$$4+4-6=\boxed{2}.$$
This verifies the cooperative debit, including both directions of every event.Addition across all gapsAfter restoring  $a_i$ , every escape U uses only tile top rows
$$a_i+2,\qquad a_i+4,\qquad a_i+6.$$
The next gap uses
$$a_i+10,\qquad a_i+12,\qquad a_i+14.$$
These tile-row sets are disjoint. The upper rotors associated with a gap lie in that same gap’s tile rows. Hence an escape U cannot create an intratile contact with a rotor or escape U from another gap.The receipts are therefore disjoint in the required senses:Each cooperative full tile belongs to one gap and one opposite pair.Each cross event retains its originating original and its ordered endpoints.Each charge contribution belongs to one distinct original.Old/old event eligibility remains unchanged because the originating support sets remain immutable.An already full tile cannot acquire a different owner at one of its cells, because endpoints of distinct originals are disjoint.Thus the escape-owner gain in the single common baseline is
$$8(g-t)+2t=8g-6t.$$
Adding the first-layer value  $5g$  proves
$$\boxed{\Phi(\text{selected})=5g+8g-6t=13g-6t\ge7g.}$$
For  $W=16$ , the choices  $k_L=k_R=6$  and  $f_L=f_R=4$  make every gap tight and give  $7g$  as a selected partial-inventory value. The endpoint records are mutually disjoint as required. This equality computation does not supply a complete extension.8. Scope of acceptance and minor wording correctionsThe accepted result is the conditional owner-forcing theorem and its exact selected-inventory identity. Its proof uses no upper bound on the dimensions and no exhaustive classification of arbitrary grid configurations.The stated boundaries remain necessary: the result does not establish complete-extension existence, complete-family sharpness, nonnegative marginal under arbitrary further originals, or a global  $5/6$  conclusion.Two wording changes would make the geometric statements literal without changing any proof:Replace “a rotor spans at most three columns” with “a rotor has column-coordinate diameter three and occupies at most four columns.”In the slack-pair argument, say the nearest outer-bar columns have coordinate difference at least three. At difference three there are two strictly intervening columns; the physical tile footprints are still disjoint.Neither is a substantive gap. The forced upper layer, the breadth-six escape-owner classification, the exceptional single-owner correction, the tight-band debit, and the simultaneous nonreuse argument all pass the written-proof audit.
